stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = 6 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 6 \) so that at time t its angle is \( \theta(t) = \frac{\pi t}{4} \), for \( 0 \le t \le 2 \). Using a calculator, find the time t at which the x-coordinate of the particle's position is 9. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The coordinate is \( x = r\cos\theta = \left(6 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 6\right) \cos{\left(\theta \right)} \), so in terms of time \( x(t) = \left(6 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} + 6\right) \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} \).
Solve \( \left(6 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} + 6\right) \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} = 9 \) on \( 0 \le t \le 2 \) with a calculator. The only solution is \( t \approx 0.769 \).

options.derivation: the equation solved in theta and the angle reported in place of the time
r treated as the x-coordinate, so the time at which r equals the value is reported
the angle rounded to one decimal place before it was converted to a time
